segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may arrange» upright «boards [passin] around a well» in the public domain in order to permit drawing water from the well on Shabbat. A well is usually at least four handbreadths wide and ten handbreadths deep. Therefore, it is considered a private domain, and it is prohibited to draw water from it on Shabbat, as that would constitute a violation of the prohibition to carry from a private domain into a public one. The Sages therefore instituted that a virtual partition may be built in the area surrounding the well, so that the enclosed area could be considered a private domain, thus permitting use of the well and carrying of the water within the partitioned area.

segments.he: אַרְבָּעָה דְּיוֹמְדִין נִרְאִין כִּשְׁמוֹנָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: שְׁמוֹנָה נִרְאִין כִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר — אַרְבָּעָה דְּיוֹמְדִים וְאַרְבָּעָה פְּשׁוּטִין.
segments.en: In this specific instance, the Sages demonstrated special leniency and did not require a proper partition to enclose the entire area. For this purpose, it suffices if there are «four double posts [deyomadin] that look like eight» single posts, i.e., four corner pieces, each comprised of two posts joined together at right angles; this is «the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Meir says:» There must be «eight» posts that «look like twelve.» How so? There must be «four double posts,» one in each corner, with «four plain» posts, one between each pair of double posts.

segments.he: גּוֹבְהָן עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְרוֹחְבָּן שִׁשָּׁה וְעוֹבְיָים כׇּל שֶׁהוּא. וּבֵינֵיהֶן כִּמְלֹא שְׁתֵּי רְבָקוֹת שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ בָּקָר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
segments.en: «The height» of the double posts must be at least «ten handbreadths, their width» must be «six» handbreadths, «and their thickness» may be even «a minimal amount. And between them,» i.e., between the posts, there may be a gap «the size of two teams [revakot] of three oxen each;» this is «the statement of Rabbi Meir.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שֶׁל אַרְבַּע, קְשׁוּרוֹת וְלֹא מוּתָּרוֹת, אַחַת נִכְנֶסֶת וְאַחַת יוֹצֵאת.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda» disagrees and «says:» There may be a slightly larger gap, the size of two teams «of four» oxen each, and this gap is measured with the cows being «tied» together «and not untied,» and with the minimal space necessary for «one» team to be «entering» while the other «one is leaving.»

segments.he: מוּתָּר לְהַקְרִיב לַבְּאֵר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁתְּהֵא פָּרָה רֹאשָׁהּ וְרוּבָּהּ בִּפְנִים וְשׁוֹתָה.
segments.en: «It is permitted to bring» the posts «closer to the well, provided that» the enclosed area is large enough for «a cow to» stand with «its head and the majority of its» body «inside» the partitioned space while «it drinks.»

segments.he: לְהַרְחִיק כׇּל שֶׁהוּא, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּרְבֶּה בְּפַסִּין. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם.
segments.en: «to distance» the boards from the well and expand the enclosed area by «any amount,» i.e., as much as one wishes, «provided that he increases the» number of upright «boards» between the double posts. «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The partitioned area may be expanded «up to» an area of «two beit se’a,» which is an area of five thousand square cubits.

segments.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא אָמְרוּ בֵּית סָאתַיִם אֶלָּא לְגִנָּה וּלְקַרְפֵּף, אֲבָל אִם הָיָה דִּיר אוֹ סַהַר אוֹ מוּקְצֶה אוֹ חָצֵר — אֲפִילּוּ בֵּית חֲמֵשֶׁת כּוֹרִין, אֲפִילּוּ בֵּית עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹרִין מוּתָּר. וּמוּתָּר לְהַרְחִיק כׇּל שֶׁהוּא, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּרְבֶּה בְּפַסִּין.
segments.en: The Rabbis «said to him: They only spoke of» an area of «two beit se’a with regard to a garden or an enclosure» used for storing wood, scrap, and the like «[karpef]. But if it was a pen [dir], or a stable [sahar], or a backyard, or a courtyard» in front of the house, «even» if it had an area of «five beit kor» or «even ten beit kor, it is permitted. And it is permitted to distance» the boards and expand the enclosed area «by any amount, provided that one increases the» upright «boards» between the double posts.
